'''{{not a typo|Andreea}} Luisa Erciulescu''' is a Romanian statistician{{r|pls}} who has worked in agricultural and [[official statistics]], [[small area estimation]], and [[survey methodology]]. She is an associate vice president for statistics and data science at [[Westat]].{{r|westat}}

==Education and career==
Erciulescu majored in mathematics at [[Colorado State University]],{{r|westat|niss}} supported by a scholarship from the Romanian government and graduating in 2011.{{r|pls}} During her studies there, she discovered an interest in statistics,{{r|niss|pls}} and won in 2010 an [[American Mathematical Society|AMS]] undergraduate poster presentation award for ''Solving [[Kakuro|Kakuro Puzzles]]''.{{r|ams}} She continued at [[Iowa State University]] for graduate study in statistics, where she received a master's degree and completed her Ph.D.,{{r|westat|niss}} in 2015.{{r|orcid}} Her dissertation, ''Small area prediction based on unit level models when the covariate mean is measured with error'', was supervised by [[Wayne Fuller]].{{r|diss}}

She was a postdoctoral researcher{{r|postdoc}} at the [[National Institute of Statistical Sciences]] from 2015 to 2018,{{r|orcid}} working there on projects associated with the [[National Agricultural Statistics Service]].{{r|niss}} In 2018 she moved to Westat as a senior statistician,{{r|orcid}} and has since become a vice president.{{r|westat}}

==Recognition==
Erciulescu is an Elected Member of the [[International Statistical Institute]].{{r|westat}} She was elected to the 2025 class of [[Fellows of the American Statistical Association]].{{r|fa}}

She was a third-place recipient of the 2022 Prize for Young Statisticians of the [[International Association for Official Statistics]], the first US-based statistician to receive this award.{{r|pys}}
